# v0.9.18 - The Review Round: a Listing That Cannot Skip, a Mark That Cannot Expire Early

## What's Changed in v0.9.18

Fixes from a three-reviewer targeted review of v0.9.17, each reproduced before it was changed. The one that matters is in payload retention: `--payload-gc --payload-delete` reads the remote's history through a "strict" listing so that a skipped ref cannot make its objects look unused, and four cases still skipped without stopping. Upgrade before running `--payload-delete` against a library with more than one branch or tag.

### Fixed
- **`--payload-gc --payload-delete` could delete a branch's objects when the helper's listing skipped the branch.** Under `SEAFILE_STRICT_REFS=1`, an entry of an unknown type, a name git refuses, a ref nested deeper than the walk goes, and a ref file that holds no object id (a torn write, an HTML error page) were skipped with a warning. The objects only that branch named were then marked and, after the grace period, deleted; reproduced against the stub, where restoring the branch failed afterwards. Each case now stops the listing and names the entry. A normal fetch or push still warns and carries on, so one planted file cannot make a repository unfetchable, and a Seafile conflict copy is still refused by retention itself before it fetches.
- **A `gc-pending.json` mark holding a time that cannot be real deleted its object on the next delete run.** A stamp of `-1` made "now minus the stamp" exceed any grace period. A stamp that is zero, negative, a boolean, not finite or more than a day ahead is now marked afresh, with a `Warning:` that says so; this only delays a deletion. A mark list that is valid JSON but not an object was read as "nothing is marked" and silently restarted every grace period; it is refused with the remedy now, as the fence baseline beside it already was.
- **`--payload-verify` fetched the whole history into the temporary volume without the free-space check `--payload-gc` has.** It makes the same check and honours `--allow-low-disk`.
- **`doctor --upload-limit` said nothing when it could not remove its scratch folder**, leaving up to 1 GiB of probe bodies on the server: `delete_entry` answers `False` for a refusal and the cleanup looked for an exception. **`doctor` printed `[ ok ] no Seafile conflict copies` when its walk had stopped at the 5,000-directory limit**; it prints a `Warning:` saying what was not looked at.

### Changed
- The refusal of a non-object `gc-seen.json` (the history-rewrite fence) had no test; removing it left the suite green. It has one.
- `ROADMAP.md` §1.6 records every finding of the review with its disposition, including the ones not acted on and why.

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. Behaviours that may surface: a `--payload-gc` / `--payload-verify` run now stops, naming the entry, when the remote's `refs/` holds a file or directory the helper cannot list as a ref (before, it carried on without that branch); a `gc-pending.json` that is not a JSON object stops `--payload-gc --payload-delete` until it is removed (removing it loses nothing and delays deletion by a full grace period); `--payload-verify` can refuse for lack of room in the temporary volume (`--allow-low-disk` overrides); `doctor` prints a `Warning:` rather than `[ ok ]` when its conflict walk reaches its limit.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
